title: IndentAtlas: an open-source toolbox for indentation mapping analysis
author: Vellwock, Amini, et al.

steps.title: Launch IndentAtlas GUI
steps.instruction: Open the provided Python script (IndentAtlas.py) and run it; after a few seconds the graphical user interface (GUI) will appear.

steps.title: Import summary data file
steps.instruction: Use Option A to select the *.txt summary file exported from the indentation instrument (e.g., Bruker/Hysitron). The file must contain the reduced modulus, hardness, etc., for every load‑displacement curve. If you have custom data, prepare an *.xlsx file following the example on the GitHub repository and do not modify the first row.

steps.title: Import optional background image
steps.instruction: Use Option B to load an image of the sample (light microscopy, SEM, etc.). If no image is chosen the background will be white.

steps.title: Define image‑datapoint alignment
steps.instruction: With Option C choose the location of the first datapoint relative to the image centre (e.g., bottom‑left, top‑right, etc.).

steps.title: Manually fine‑tune alignment
steps.instruction: If needed, adjust the alignment using Option D: apply x‑ or y‑axis shifts, rotation, and/or scaling to match the image and the indentation grid.

steps.title: Import individual load‑displacement curves
steps.instruction: Option E allows selection of one or more *.txt files containing raw curves. Each file must have depth in the first column and load in the second column; reformat other manufacturers’ files accordingly (see example files on GitHub). This step is optional.

steps.title: Specify points to keep or discard
steps.instruction: In Option F enter point IDs to remove or to keep, using commas (e.g., “1,2,3”) or ranges (e.g., “1-100”).

steps.title: Apply tip‑calibration filter
steps.instruction: Check Option G to retain only datapoints whose contact depth lies within the user‑defined tip calibration range (e.g., 4 nm – 220 nm).

steps.title: Set visualization parameters
steps.instruction: Adjust the following options as desired: font size (H), bin factor for spatial averaging (I), marker size (J), marker shape – circle for conical tips, triangle‑down for Berkovich tips (K), map colour scale (L), clustering colour scale (M).

steps.title: Define property limits
steps.instruction: Enter minimum and maximum values for reduced modulus (Option N) and for hardness (Option O) to restrict the data shown in maps.

steps.title: Configure k‑means clustering
steps.instruction: Set the desired number of clusters with Option P, optionally tick Option Q to export a *.txt file containing basic clustering statistics.

steps.title: Set outlier detection threshold
steps.instruction: In Option R specify how many standard deviations (σ) from the mean of the selected variable (reduced modulus or hardness) a datapoint must lie to be flagged as an outlier.

steps.title: Export analysis results
steps.instruction: Use Option S to generate a *.txt file with overall statistics (mean, min, max, etc.), Option T for a cleaned data file (after point removal), and Option U for a *.txt log of all GUI inputs.

steps.title: Generate standard plots
steps.instruction: Select the following options to visualise data: reduced modulus, hardness and contact‑depth distributions with outliers (V); k‑means clustering maps, elbow and silhouette plots, scatter‑box plots (W); all load‑vs‑displacement curves (X); map plots without background (Y); map plots with background image (Z).

steps.title: Example workflow: mantis‑shrimp sample
steps.instruction: After loading the summary *.txt (Option A) and optical image (Option B), set alignment to bottom‑left (Option C). Import selected curves (Option E) and view them (Option X). Exclude curves outside the tip calibration range 4–220 nm (Option G). Plot remaining points (Option V) to identify statistical outliers; manually remove extreme IDs (e.g., 121) using Option F. Re‑plot the cleaned map (Option V). Perform k‑means clustering with two clusters (Option P) and view elbow, silhouette and cluster maps (Option W). Export clustering results (Option Q) and GUI log (Option U).

steps.title: Example workflow: locust valve sample
steps.instruction: Load the hardness summary file (Option A) and plot a hardness map (Option Y). Remove datapoints outside the calibration range (Option G); they typically appear at the sample‑epoxy interface. Manually select out‑of‑sample points with box or lasso tools and delete them via Option F. Apply spatial binning with a factor of two or three (Option I) to obtain smoother maps (Option Y). Change marker shape to triangle‑down to represent Berkovich tips (Option K).

steps.title: Example workflow: titanium dataset
steps.instruction: Convert the original *.mat file to the *.xlsx format matching the example column order (see GitHub). Import the converted file (Option A) and generate a hardness map (Option Y). Select a region of interest with Option F, then run k‑means clustering with two clusters (Option P) and view the silhouette score (Option W). Export the clustering file (Option Q) and the GUI input log (Option U).
